- Clicking on the blob moves the absorbed square to that clicked position
- Blob grew from 65 to 67 pixels (+2)
- Square moved from (26, 36) [right side] to (22, 32) [top side]

Now I need to figure out the goal. The square can be moved to any position on the blob's boundary. The blob is at (23-31, 29-37), so the square can be moved to positions around this region.
Looking at the other squares:
- (33, 14) - left side, can't reach blob
- (53, 44) - right side, can reach blob by moving up-left
- (56, 15) - left side, can't reach blob
Maybe the goal is to move the absorbed square to a specific position on the blob, like the center or a corner? Or maybe the goal is to use the blob to "push" the square into one of the other squares?
Actually, let me think about this differently. The blob has one absorbed square. When I click on the blob, the square moves to that position. Maybe the goal is to move the square to a position where it can be "released" or "dropped" somewhere specific?
Or maybe the goal is to absorb ALL squares into the blob, and then arrange them in a specific pattern?
Let me try clicking on the blob to absorb the square at (53, 44), which is the closest to the blob. If the blob absorbs the closest square, then after absorbing (53, 44), the blob would have 2 squares inside it.
But wait, the blob already has one square inside it (the one I've been moving around). If I click on the blob to absorb another square, what happens to the first one?
Let me test this by clicking on the blob center to see if it absorbs the square at (53, 44).
Actually, first let me check: the square at (53, 44) is at row 53, column 44. The blob is at rows 23-31, columns 29-37. The distance is about 22 rows and 7 columns. This is much farther than the previous absorption, where the square was only 2 rows away.
So maybe the blob can only absorb squares that are within a certain range. Let me first move the square at (53, 44) closer to the blob, then try to absorb it.
But wait, I've been wasting actions moving the absorbed square around the blob. Maybe the goal is just to absorb all squares, and the "moving" mechanic is just a side effect of clicking on the blob.
Let me try a different approach: move the square at (53, 44) closer to the blob, then click on the blob to absorb it.
